learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the 'language of business'! Understand how businesses record, classify, and summarize their financial data to make smart decisions.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Accounting is the art of recording, classifying, and summarizing financial transactions. Just like you keep a diary of your daily life, a business keeps an accounting diary to track its money.

Many people read accounting reports! Internal users (owners, managers) use them to run the business. External users (banks, government, investors) use them to decide if the business is safe to invest in or lend to.
Assets are things the business OWNS (like cash, machinery, or buildings). Liabilities are things the business OWES to outsiders (like bank loans or unpaid bills).
Capital is the money or assets the owner brings into the business. According to the Accounting Equation, Assets = Liabilities + Capital.

fun_activity.title: 🎒 The Backpack Audit
fun_activity.instructions: Empty your school backpack. Everything inside it that you own (books, pens, lunchbox) is your 'Asset'. Did you borrow a pen from a friend? That is your 'Liability'. The total value of your own stuff is your 'Capital'!

exam_tips: 📌 Know the exact difference between Book-keeping (routine recording of data) and Accounting (summarizing and interpreting data).
📌 Distinguish between Debtors (people who owe US money) and Creditors (people WE owe money to).
📌 Remember the basic Accounting Equation: $A = L + C$. You will get at least one numerical question on this.
quick_recap: ⭐ Accounting identifies, measures, records, and communicates financial information.
⭐ An asset is an economic resource expected to benefit future operations.
⭐ Revenue increases capital, while expenses and drawings decrease capital.
